objects.summary: Q7/Q8 delivered and references bound; L2-J remains LOT2_PREPARATION_COMPLETE_WITH_LOCAL_BLOCKERS, not READY_FOR_ASTRA_LOT3. Builder recommends launching Astra despite missing VM L2-A because the mission treats it as a known gap; no Owner decision expressed.
Parallel Q13/Q14 assigned while Astra launch proceeds; efficiency law repeated: bounded reads, no full-history subagent, class A only, no Owner decision.
Astra lot 3 is now a fact: launched at 00:58Z. P2 planning handed to Codex; VM/reserve remain Owner-gated and no new authority is created.
Owner asks Codex to challenge initiative imbalance, duplicate work, expensive-model misuse and passive-review behavior; authorization is to propose/contest, not to decide reserved matters.

Codex proposes Q13 closed-domain structural_linkage_status, Q14 adversarial triage, and P2 queue. D1 stays closed, E ineffective, VM unqualified, lot-4 real-config permissive evaluation forbidden until prerequisites. Planning explicitly reconnects A2 to economic value rather than governance activity.

Controller republishes Q13/Q14 byte-identically and raises one substantive objection: producer-vs-verifier handling of INDETERMINATE must be explicit so out-of-domain producer output cannot be silently normalized. T0 handling for unbounded validate_binding is retained.
Builder corrects an independence overstatement: Q13 had been read; only the independent 15-item inventory source remained separate. Erratum preserved rather than rewriting history.

Codex diagnoses loop inefficiency: Claude had led most initiative; both agents duplicated reads and over-optimized governance. Three corrections proposed: alternating initiative, deterministic/mechanical work separated from reasoning, and an economic-value gate for future tasks. First challenge task P2-C1 is assigned immediately.

cross_object_findings.finding: Astra lot 3 launch occurred while VM L2-A remained unqualified; this was an explicit known-gap review strategy, not evidence that the VM gap was closed.
Q13/Q14 add reusable fail-closed design: closed domain, exact guarded-content inventory and adversarial triage, while preserving D1 closed and all activation boundaries.

Historical team itself identified the same productivity failure later found by forensic audit: initiative concentrated in one agent, duplicate reads, narrative rechecks and activity optimized over economic information. Proposed remedy is alternating initiative, deterministic automation and an economic-value gate.
Independence claim about the 15-item inventory was corrected in a new comment rather than retroactively rewritten, preserving the evidence chain.
